text:
Nora: Quick gut-check — running into cases where a missing safetensors index stalls warmup. Thinking we should add a lightweight "gating" in the loader: if header/index missing or corrupted, immediately fall back to tarball stream and continue warmup rather than retrying/pausing.
Tomas: +1. Seen this with partial uploads from the artifact pipeline. Right now the hotstart waits forever for an index that never arrives.
Rachel: Is the proposal to make fallback the default path, or only trigger after N seconds/attempts? We need to be careful with silent fallbacks for customers expecting optimized safetensors semantics.
Nora: Prefer deterministic: check header checksum + presence of index. If index absent -> fallback path. No time-based heuristics. We'll emit an alert metric and a trace that links to the artifact ID.
Sam: From infra side — that approach avoids long backoffs. But we should preserve a flag in the model metadata indicating fallback happened so we can surface to users (and metrics).
Leah: Caller-side API implications? Do we need to change the WeightSource interface? Currently it returns a single Response stream.
Tomas: Minimal change: WeightSource exposes metadata map earlier in the handshake. Loader can inspect metadata.index_present boolean. If false -> route to tarball reader internally. No change to callers beyond extra fields in logs.
Rachel: We should add a small contract: metadata.index_present is authoritative only for on-disk artifacts. For S3/remote we validate by reading header bytes. If mismatch, mark index_present=false.
Nora: Implementation sketch:
```
header = read_header(obj)
if not header.get('index_offset'):
  emit_metric('safetensors.index_missing')
  loader = TarballFallbackLoader(obj)
else:
  loader = SafetensorsLoader(obj)
return loader.stream()
```
Leah: What about partial index (corrupt checksum)? Same story: treat as missing and fallback. But log full checksum and keep a short pointer in trace for debugging.
Sam: Ops concern: if artifact producer keeps pushing broken safetensors, fallback will increase CPU (tarball parsing) cost. We should rate-limit repeated fallbacks per artifact and add a remediation ticket.
Nora: Good call. Add a per-artifact fallback counter metric + burn-in throttle: after 3 fallbacks in 12h, mark artifact as quarantined and route subsequent requests to older pinned checkpoints if available.
Tomas: Also consider cold-cache warmup ordering: when fallback happens we should deprioritize full tarball warmup to avoid OOMs — prefer streaming tokenized layers first. Implementation detail for runtime team.
Rachel: I'll take a tiny RFC addendum for the loader handshake and metrics (1 page). Nora can put a short PR with the guard + tests.
Nora: I'll open the PR with unit tests and an integration that simulates an index-missing artifact. @dev-bot can we add an alert rule when safetensors.index_missing > 0 and fallback_count_per_artifact > 3?
dev-bot: Acknowledged. Created alert stub: SAFETENSORS_INDEX_MISSING (severity: low) — will link to the RFC once Rachel posts it.
Leah: One more UX note: console should show "Fallback to legacy weights (safetensors index missing)" in the model load timeline, so customers see why perf regressed.
Sam: Added a TODO in infra: retention window for fallback counters = 30d. Also add a runbook link in the alert.
Nora: Thanks everyone — plan: Rachel RFC, Nora PR, Sam + Ops add alert and retention. We'll review in next eng-ml sync if no blockers.
Rachel: sounds good :+1:
Tomas: thanks — happy path looks straightforward.
